s01.headline: I was at Jantar Mantar 1.0.
s01.headline2: If you’re going for 2.0, here’s what I want you to know.
s01.deck: What police have actually been doing, how to protect yourself and each other, and how to make them answer for it.

s02.headline: Before you leave, know what’s changed.
s02.foot: The protest does not have police permission. Going is your decision. Make it with current information.

s03.headline: Don’t plan for the rules. Plan for what’s been happening.
s03.lede: These are from the last few weeks at and around Jantar Mantar. Some are allegations under inquiry. All of them were reported.
items: Officers with no name tags
Journalists asked why on 2 Oct and were refused an answer. The law says they must wear one when arresting.
The Wire, 5 Oct
Women taken after dark, in unmarked cars
A student leader says she was driven to Narela in a private-looking car with no woman officer.
The Wire, The Quint, 5–6 Oct
Groping and stripping allegations
Three women journalists allege sexual harassment by police. One names an ACP. Another says officers lifted her shirt on a bus.
The Wire, The Quint, ABC
No FIR without video
Police told the complainants an FIR would follow only if video evidence emerged.
The Quint, 6 Oct
Cameras and phones snatched
Reporters describe cameras, mics, phones and glasses torn away during detention.
The Quint, 6 Oct
Batons and tear gas
On 20 July police used both. Police counted about 60 protesters injured.
NPR, TIME, July

s04.headline: Your phone may stop connecting. Prepare before it does.
s04.testimony: At Jantar Mantar 1.0 in July, communication was a real problem for me, and I found 112 unreliable.
s04.confirmed: Mobile internet is reported suspended within about 4 km of Jantar Mantar until 10 pm on 10 Oct.
s04.unverified: Claims that calls will be jammed have not been verified. Plan as if they might be.
steps: Download this guide while you’re still connected.
Write two numbers on your arm in marker: family and legal aid 15100.
Lock your phone with a PIN. Turn off face and fingerprint unlock.
Tell family you may be unreachable for hours.
Agree a check-in time and a meeting point.
Carry cash. UPI and cab apps need data.
Know how you’ll get home without an app.

s05.headline: Carry what you’d need if the day goes wrong.
items: Water
More than you think
Food and ORS
Something that won’t spoil
Your medicines
And a note of any condition you have
Power bank
Charged tonight
Phone locked with a PIN
Not face or fingerprint
Marker pen
For numbers on your arm and notes
Cash
Enough to get home from the edge of the city
Basic ID
Only what you need
Shoes you can move in
You may walk far, or fast
Spare glasses
Reporters lost theirs in the scuffles
Your access needs
Mobility aids, personal care, sanitary supplies
s05.note: Leave behind anything you can’t afford to lose. Don’t go without medicine, care or support you need.

s06.headline: Don’t be alone there. Not for a minute.
body: Go in pairs or small groups. Know each other’s full name, a family number, and any medical condition.
Agree this now: if one of you is taken, the other notes the time, the place, the vehicle number and which way it went, shouts their name so others hear it, and calls family and legal aid.
If you see a woman alone being pulled away, don’t look away. Film it, say her name if you know it, stay close, and get her a number.
s06.boundary_label: Friendly is not the same as trusting.
s06.boundary: You don’t owe anyone your number or your company. Don’t go anywhere with a stranger, in uniform or not.
s06.close: People who were strangers in the morning can still choose to look out for each other.

s07.kicker: 07 · If someone puts their hands on you
s07.headline: If you’re grabbed, groped or stripped, make it loud.
steps: Shout what is happening
Say it in plain words. “He is touching me.” “Where is the woman officer?” Noise brings cameras and witnesses.
Make people look
Ask anyone near you to film. Ask witnesses for their names and numbers.
Get their identity
Name tag, rank, helmet number, vehicle number. If there’s no name tag, say so out loud on camera. The law requires one when arresting. BNSS s. 36
Demand a woman officer
Only a woman may search a woman. A woman should not be arrested after sunset without a magistrate’s permission. BNSS s. 49, 43(5)
Don’t hit back
Not because they deserve calm. Because hitting back becomes their case against you, and your complaint becomes harder.
s07.after: It was not your fault. Tell someone you trust tonight, and turn to slide 10 for what to do next.

s08.headline: If they put you in a bus.
steps: Shout your name and a number
As you’re taken, shout your full name and a family number so people outside can trace you.
Show it through the window
A reporter on 4 Oct wrote what was happening and a phone number on paper and held it up for friends outside.
Ask where you’re being taken
“Kis thane le ja rahe ho?” Repeat the answer to everyone around you.
Say any medical condition at once
Loudly, to officers and others on board. Diabetes, asthma, pregnancy, anything.
Don’t unlock your phone
They may take it. Keep it locked. SFLC.in has a guide on device seizure.
Stay with the group
Resist being split into a separate private car alone. Ask for a woman officer and a marked vehicle.
s08.expect: In recent protests, many people were held for hours at police stations or stadiums, then released in the evening, sometimes far from where they were picked up. Keep cash for the journey back.
s08.outside: Call legal aid 15100 and their family. Go to the police station they were taken to. Ask for the arrest memo if they were arrested. Don’t post their private details.

s09.headline: They go for cameras first. Record anyway.

cols.label: Record
items: Film from a safe distance, in short clips.
Get faces, name tags or their absence, helmet and vehicle numbers.
Capture before and after, not only the peak.
Say the date, time and place out loud.

cols.label: Preserve
items: Pass clips to a friend away from the front line.
Keep the original file, with sound. Don’t trim or filter it.
Back it up the moment you have a connection.

cols.label: Publish with care
items: Think about faces of people who could be harmed.
Show a lawyer first if it may be evidence.

s09.impersonation: Police told the 3 Oct complainants an FIR would follow only with video. Your footage may be the only evidence someone has.
s09.close: A complete record can matter long after the moment has passed.

s10.headline: The law may not protect you on the day. Use it after.
steps: Write it all down tonight
Times, places, names, badge or helmet numbers, words used, who saw it.
Get a medical examination
Go to a government hospital. Ask for a medico-legal case (MLC). Photograph every injury.
File in writing at any police station
Get a stamped receiving copy. A Zero FIR can be filed at any station. BNSS s. 173(1)
If they refuse
Send it in writing to the DCP, then apply to a magistrate. BNSS s. 173(4), 175(3)
Complain beyond the police
National Commission for Women (14490, ncwapps.nic.in) · Delhi Police Complaints Authority for detention without due process or custodial abuse (011 2140 0977)
Get a lawyer
Free legal aid 15100, or the organisations on slide 11.
s10.note: Refusing to register some sexual-offence complaints is itself an offence for an officer. BNS s. 199(c). Ask a lawyer how it applies to yours.
s10.disclaimer: General information, not legal advice. Have a lawyer check your case.

s11.headline: Numbers to have on paper.
s11.honest: As of 9 Oct, 9:40 pm, I haven’t confirmed any independent lawyer, doctor or volunteer on the ground for 10 Oct. If you are one, message me and I’ll verify and add you, with your consent.

s12.headline: I hope everyone gets home safe.
s12.body: You’ll be angry tomorrow, and you’ll have every reason. Be loud. Just don’t be alone, and don’t hand them an excuse. Record everything. And if something happens to you or to the person next to you, it doesn’t end when the bus doors open. Write it down, get it examined, file it, and keep going until someone answers for it.

1.headline: I was at Jantar Mantar 1.0 in July.
1.body: If you’re going for 2.0 tomorrow, I’ve put together what you actually need: what police have been doing, what to do if you’re grabbed or put in a bus, how to keep evidence, and how to make them answer for it afterwards.
1.cta: Full guide on my profile. Save it while you have signal.

2.headline: Do these tonight.
items: Write family and 15100 on your arm.
Lock your phone with a PIN, not your face.
Pair up. Swap full names and numbers.
Agree a check-in time and place.
Pack cash, water, medicines, spare glasses.
Tell family you may be unreachable.
